_readme: Every grant below ships OFF. Turn one on only when you mean it, and put the
date you decided in granted_on -- the run records that date in its log, which
is what makes an unattended submit auditable months later.
submit_when_clean is the big one. With it off, the pipeline fills forms and
stops, and you click Submit yourself. That is the recommended default: some
ATS terms of service prohibit automated submission, and the decision to
accept that risk is yours to make deliberately, not to inherit from an
Turning submit_when_clean on does NOT mean 'always submit'. The run still
refuses whenever a value was guessed, a required field is empty, a validation
error is showing, the generic resume got attached where a tailored one was
expected, or an account was created this session. Those refusals are the
point of the pipeline; the grant only removes the per-application prompt.

submit_when_clean.note: fill and stop; you press Submit

create_accounts.note: sign up when a portal has no existing account

outreach_auto_send.note: send drafts unattended; highest ban risk, leave off until calibrated
